title: IU vs UMN: tuition, size, location
summary: Indiana University-Bloomington (IU) versus University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN). Also searched as UMN vs IU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: The University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) and Indiana University-Bloomington (IU) are both public institutions but differ in several key aspects. UMN has an undergraduate enrollment of 31,855 students, while IU enrolls 37,806 undergraduates. Tuition for in-state students at UMN is $17,214, which is higher compared to IU's in-state tuition of $12,144. Geographically, UMN is located in Minneapolis, Minnesota, whereas IU is situated in Bloomington, Indiana. These differences highlight variations in size, cost, and location between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance, the University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) and Indiana University-Bloomington (IU) show distinct differences. UMN's in-state tuition is $17,214, which is higher than IU's in-state tuition of $12,144. For out-of-state students, UMN charges $38,362, while IU's out-of-state tuition is $41,891, making IU more expensive for non-residents. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at UMN is $19,500, closely matching IU's median debt of $19,509. These figures illustrate that while UMN has higher in-state tuition, IU has higher out-of-state tuition, with both institutions having nearly identical median student debt levels.

In summary, UMN vs IU reveals that in-state students may find IU more affordable, whereas out-of-state students might face higher costs at IU. The median debt for graduates from both universities remains comparable, reflecting similar financial outcomes for students completing their degrees.

sections.heading: Pick UMN if
paragraphs: When deciding between the University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) and Indiana University-Bloomington (IU), prospective students might pick UMN if they prioritize a public university with a higher completion rate.
